newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian sport worried by loss of tobacco ads.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian sport worried by loss of tobacco ads.

text.p: Slovenian sport and cultural organisations said on Friday a new law prohibiting tobacco advertising may seriously hamper their work.

"We are not against the law but sport organisations will lose a significant amount of their income because of it," Marjan Jemec, deputy general secretar of the Slovenian Olympic Committee, told Reuters.

On Wednesday the Slovenian parliament passed a law prohibiting the advertising of tobacco products and brand names, except within 15 days of launching a new line. The law will come into effect next month.
Jemec said Slovenian sport organisations relied on tobacco advertising for about five percent of their revenue. She added that kayaking, car racing, tennis and skiing.
Sport and cultural organisations said they expected the government to make up for the loss by granting them additional money from the budget.
"We hope the government will find additional financial sources," said Vojko Stopar, secretary of the Association of Slovenian Cultural Organisations.
